info.title: vatnode API
info.summary: EU VAT validation and rates API
info.description:
vatnode validates EU VAT IDs against the EU Commission’s VIES system with
national-database fallback, and serves up-to-date VAT rates for every
EU member state. Coverage: all 27 EU member states + Northern Ireland (XI prefix),
which participates in VIES under the Windsor Framework.

This specification covers two surfaces:

- The **product API** – VAT validation (`/v1/vat/*`) and VAT rates
  (`/v1/rates/*`), authenticated with an API key. This is the surface you
  integrate against from your backend.
- The **account-management API** – profile and API keys (`/v1/me/*`),
  authenticated with the logged-in browser session. These endpoints power
  the vatnode dashboard and are not intended for API-key-authenticated
  server-to-server use.
- **VAT monitoring** – subscriptions (`/v1/subscriptions/*`) and webhook
  registration (`/v1/webhooks/*`), which accept either the dashboard
  session or a live API key, so integrations such as the Zapier and Make
  apps can subscribe to VAT events on the account’s behalf.

Billing endpoints (`/v1/billing/*`) remain internal to the dashboard and
are not part of this contract.

## Authentication

`/v1/vat/*` requires an API key passed as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer vat_live_...
```

Test keys (prefix `vat_test_`) accept only VAT IDs starting with `XX` and
return deterministic fixtures without hitting VIES or consuming quota.

`/v1/rates/*` is public and requires no authentication.

The account-management endpoints (`/v1/me/*`) are authenticated by the
better-auth session cookie (`better-auth.session_token`) set when a user
logs in to the dashboard. They do not accept API-key bearer tokens. A
request without a valid session returns `401 UNAUTHORIZED`.

Monitoring (`/v1/subscriptions/*`) and webhook registration
(`/v1/webhooks/*`) accept either that session cookie or a **live** API key
as a Bearer token. A test key is rejected with `403 TEST_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED`,
because these endpoints act on real VAT numbers and deliver real HTTP
callbacks.

`/v1/account` returns the plan, quota and billing state of the account a
key belongs to. It spends no quota and accepts test keys, so integrations
use it both as their connection test and to show entitlements.

## Errors

Every error response uses the same envelope:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "STABLE_CODE", "message": "…", "requestId": "…" } }
```

`code` is a stable machine-readable string (branch on it, not on
`message`); `message` is human-readable and may change; `requestId` echoes
the `X-Request-Id` response header for support correlation. The full set of
`code` values is enumerated on the `VatError` and `ManagementError` schemas.

Two conditions apply to every operation and are not repeated on each one:

- Any request whose body, query or path parameters fail structural
  validation returns `400` with code `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- Any unexpected server-side failure returns `500` with code
  `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Consultation numbers

When your account has a requester VAT configured (dashboard Account details →
Requester VAT, or `PATCH /v1/me/requester`), every call to
`/v1/vat/{vatId}` automatically calls VIES `checkVatApprox` on behalf of
that requester. VIES then returns a `consultationNumber` (its own
`requestIdentifier`) in the response. It proves a check was made against
VIES at a given date and time – it shows that you checked, not that the
counterparty stayed valid afterwards.

The requester is account-level only – there is no per-call override.
Configure it once and it applies to every subsequent check.

When a requester is configured, vatnode guarantees one of two outcomes:
a successful response containing a `consultationNumber`, or an error.
National-registry fallback is disabled in this mode – a result without
a consultation number would silently strip the audit evidence the
account opted into. Specifically:

- If VIES rejects the requester (e.g. deregistered, typo), the API
  returns `INVALID_REQUESTER` (HTTP 422).
- If VIES is unavailable, the API returns `VIES_UNAVAILABLE`
  (HTTP 503) or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (HTTP 504) – no national
  fallback is attempted.

Accounts that prefer maximum validation availability over a consultation
number on every check should leave the requester unset.

## What a `checkId` guarantees

Every successful validation returns a `checkId`, and it is only issued
after the check has been committed to vatnode’s own records. There is no
window in which you hold a `checkId` for a check vatnode cannot produce,
for as long as we retain the record – check records are anonymised after
five years, and de-linked from the account when it is deleted.
If the record cannot be written, the call fails with `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED`
(HTTP 502) instead of returning a verdict – nothing is billed, and the
request is safe to retry. The same rule covers a bulk job’s positions: a
position whose record cannot be written reports `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED`
instead of a verdict, and is not billed.

get.description:
Validates the supplied VAT ID against VIES, falling back to the
relevant national registry when VIES is unavailable. Without a
requester, for some member states vatnode also queries the national
VAT register at the same time as VIES, and the register answer is
returned if it arrives first – `source` is then the register code and
`consultationNumber` is `null`. Results for the base validation are cached for up to 15
minutes.

Configure a requester VAT once in the dashboard (Account details, or
`PATCH /v1/me/requester`) to obtain a VIES `consultationNumber`
on every call automatically. When the account has a requester
configured, the cache is bypassed so a fresh consultation number is
always issued.

valid.summary: Valid VAT ID with consultation number

value.companyAddress: 3RD FLOOR, GORDON HOUSE, BARROW STREET, DUBLIN 4

specialTerritory.summary: Valid VAT ID whose address falls in a special territory
specialTerritory.description:
A mainland trader – almost every result – has
`specialTerritory: null`, as above. This is what the field
looks like when the trader address says otherwise.

400.description:
The VAT ID is not a valid VAT number format (`INVALID_FORMAT`).
In test mode, a VAT ID not starting with `XX` also returns
`INVALID_FORMAT`.

403.description:
VIES reported the VAT ID or your IP as blocked
(`VAT_BLOCKED` / `IP_BLOCKED`). Surfaced as `VIES_ERROR`.

422.description:
The account’s configured requester VAT (dashboard setting) is
invalid in VIES. Only returned when a requester is configured.
Fix or clear it to continue.

502.description:
VIES returned an unexpected protocol error. Also returned when a
requester is configured and VIES answered `valid: true` without a
consultation number (retried once first) – the check is withheld
rather than delivered without its audit evidence, and no quota is
consumed.

`AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED` is the third case: the check itself succeeded,
but its record could not be stored, so the verdict and its `checkId`
are withheld rather than handed back unrecorded. No quota is
consumed and the check is safe to retry.

503.description:
VIES is unavailable. Without a requester, vatnode also
exhausted national-registry fallbacks. With a requester,
national fallback is intentionally skipped.

504.description: VIES request timed out and no fallback was available.

post.summary: Submit up to 50 000 EU VAT IDs for background validation
post.description:
Records the batch and answers `202 Accepted` with a job id. **Nothing is
validated during this request** – the positions are worked through in
the background and read back through the three endpoints below.

This is why the endpoint is asynchronous: a cold-cache VAT ID costs a
real VIES round trip, so even a hundred of them cannot honestly be
answered inside one HTTP request, let alone fifty thousand. A job runs
at a deliberately limited concurrency – five checks at a time, whatever
the batch size – and steps aside from member states VIES is currently
struggling with, so a batch takes a bounded share of upstream capacity
rather than as much as it can get. There is no priority queue: your live
`GET /v1/vat/{vatId}` calls are not routed ahead of your batches, they
simply are not competing with an unbounded one. Stepping aside applies
to the affected positions only: the job keeps working every other member
state in the batch and comes back to the degraded one later. If it is
still degraded when the job runs out of retries, ONLY that member
state’s positions are answered `VIES_UNAVAILABLE` – a position is never
given an error for a check that was not attempted.

**Duplicates are collapsed.** VAT IDs are normalised (trimmed,
uppercased) and de-duplicated, preserving first-seen order, so a list
containing the same ID twice produces ONE position and is charged ONE
quota unit. `duplicatesDropped` reports how many entries that removed.

**Send an `Idempotency-Key`.** It is optional, and this is the endpoint
where it matters most: if the connection drops before the `202` arrives,
you cannot tell whether up to 50 000 billable positions were accepted,
and a plain retry buys them twice. Repeating the request with the same
key AND THE SAME LIST OF VAT IDS returns the SAME job – no second job,
no second charge. Keys are scoped to your account; a key you have not
used before starts a new batch. Repeating a key with a DIFFERENT list is
rejected with `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` rather than silently
answered with the old job (which would hide part of the new batch) or
bought as a second job (which would defeat the key). 8–200 characters of
letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `_`; a key that does not parse is refused
with `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID` rather than ignored, because ignoring it
would leave you believing you were protected.

**Quota is spent per position, as it is answered**, exactly as on the
single-ID endpoint – not reserved for the whole batch up front. A
position that ends in an upstream error is refunded, and so is one
whose answer could not be stored. That per-position accounting has
one gap: if the process running the job dies between reserving a
position’s quota and recording its answer, the reservation is not
returned. The position stays pending, is answered again when the job
resumes, and its quota unit is spent twice – bounded by the five
positions a pass works on at once, so a crash costs at most a
handful of positions, not the batch. What running out of quota
mid-job does depends on the plan: a plan with overage enabled keeps
going and bills the extra positions at its overage rate, while a
hard-capped plan answers every remaining position with
`RATE_LIMITED`. Either way the job finishes.

In test mode (a `vat_test_` key) the job is real and the polling
contract is identical, but every position must start with `XX` and is
answered from fixtures – no quota, no VIES call, no stored check.

Jobs and their positions are kept for **30 days** (`expiresAt`), after
which they are deleted. The checks themselves live on under their own
`checkId` in your check history.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Mint one per batch you intend to submit (a UUID is ideal) and resend
it verbatim, with the same `vatIds`, on any retry. The same key and
batch always resolve to the same job; the same key with a different
batch is a `409`, not a silent mismatch.

202.description:
The batch was recorded. Poll the job for progress. A repeat of a
request that carried an `Idempotency-Key` and the SAME `vatIds`
answers `202` with the job that key already created – `status` and
the counters are then whatever that job has reached by now, not
recomputed from this request, and not necessarily `queued`.

409.description:
This `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different batch
(`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`). The job it originally bought is
untouched; resubmit with a new key to run this batch.

get.summary: Read a bulk job’s status and progress
get.description:
Progress counters are kept on the job itself, so this stays a single
cheap read however large the batch is. Poll it until `status` is
terminal – `finished`, `cancelled` or `failed` – then page through the
results. Every job reaches one of the three: there is a bound on how
many times a job may step aside from a degraded member state, and on
the last attempt the affected positions are answered rather than
postponed again.

get.summary: Page through a bulk job’s positions
get.description:
Positions in submit order, readable while the job is still running —
a position that is not answered yet has `status: pending`. Each answered
position carries the same `checkId` as the equivalent single check, so
it is traceable to a stored record.

On a `cancelled` job, `pending` is final: those positions were never
checked, never charged, and will never be answered. Resubmit the ones
you still need as a new batch.

post.summary: Ask a running bulk job to stop
post.description:
Idempotent. The job stops at its next position and ends `cancelled`;
positions already answered keep their result and stay billed – the
check ran and its record exists. Positions it had not reached stay
`pending` for good and are not charged. Cancelling an already-finished
job changes nothing and returns it as it stands.

Revoking the API key a job was submitted with stops it the same way:
revocation means nothing more is read or written with that key, and a
running batch is no exception. Such a job ends `cancelled` with
`errorCode: API_KEY_REVOKED`. Everything it had already collected stays
readable through your other keys and in your check history.

200.description: The job as it now stands.

get.summary: List VAT rates for all European countries

200.description:
List of VAT rates for all 45 European countries: EU-27, Northern
Ireland (XI), and non-EU countries (e.g. Norway, Switzerland, the
United Kingdom, Ukraine, Turkey). The `isEU` flag distinguishes
member states. These are reference rates only – VAT number
validation covers EU-27 + Northern Ireland.

404.description:
The path is not recognised. `GET /v1/rates` takes no parameters and
requires no authentication, so it produces no client error of its
own; the API’s global handler returns the standard `NOT_FOUND`
envelope only for an unrecognised path under the rates namespace
(for example a mistyped `/v1/rates/{code}`).

get.summary: Get VAT rates for a single country

parameters.name: countryCode
parameters.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (uppercase). Use `GR` for Greece —
the VAT prefix `EL` is **not** accepted on this endpoint and returns
`404`. Northern Ireland is `XI`.

400.description:
The `countryCode` path segment is not exactly two letters
(`INVALID_REQUEST`). A well-formed but unknown code returns `404`
instead.

get.summary: Account summary for the calling API key
get.description:
Plan entitlements, quota consumption, monitoring usage and billing
state for the account the key belongs to. Read-only and local: it never
calls VIES, never contacts the payment provider and never spends
quota, so an integration can poll it cheaply and use it as its
connection test – an invalid or revoked key returns `401`.

Test keys are accepted, so a customer can wire up an integration
against the sandbox before switching to a live key.

Carries no personal data: an API key identifies an account, not a
person.

200.description: Entitlements and consumption for the account.

label.description: Human-readable key label set in the dashboard.

subscriptionsLimit.description: Monitored VAT IDs allowed. `-1` = unlimited, `0` = not available on this plan.

webhooksLimit.description: Webhook endpoints allowed. `-1` = unlimited, `0` = not available on this plan.

used.description: Validations spent in the current quota window.

limit.description: Same as `plan.monthlyQuota`, repeated so a client needs one field.

remaining.description:
Validations left inside the included quota, floored at 0. `-1`
on an unlimited plan. Checks continue past 0 where the plan
allows overage – this is not a hard stop.

overage.description: Validations beyond the included quota in this window.

resetAt.description: When the quota window rolls over, anchored to the signup day-of-month.

monitoring.description:
Current consumption against the plan’s monitoring limits, counted
the same way those limits are enforced on create.

status.description: Subscription state. `null` on a free account.

interval.description: Billing cadence. `null` when there is no paid subscription.

currentPeriodEnd.description: End of the paid period. `null` on a free account.

nextChargeAt.description:
When the subscription renews. `null` unless the status is
`active` — a cancelling subscription runs to the end of the
period and is not charged again.

get.description: Profile, plan and current-period usage for the authenticated user.

200.description: The authenticated user’s profile, plan and usage.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the authenticated user’s account: revokes all live API
keys immediately, invalidates all sessions, and anonymises the email
after a 30-day grace period. Idempotency is not offered – a second
call returns `409 ALREADY_DELETED`.

409.description: Account is already scheduled for deletion (`ALREADY_DELETED`).

get.description:
Current billing-period request usage (included + overage), lifetime
request total and monitoring-subscription usage against plan limits.

200.description: Usage statistics for the current billing period.
Account-level email-alert settings for VAT monitoring.

patch.description:
Toggle email alerts and/or set the target address. Pass an empty
string for `email` to clear the override and fall back to the account
email.

email.description: A valid email address, or an empty string to clear the override.

get.summary: Render a sample monitoring digest email
get.description:
Returns a representative alert email (subject, HTML and text) so the
user can preview exactly what a monitoring digest looks like.

The last 20 sign-in / signup and API-key audit events for the
authenticated user, merged and sorted newest-first. Drives the
‘Recent activity’ card in the dashboard.
Paginated history of VAT checks made with the account’s API keys (50 per page).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Invalid or missing values default to 1.

200.description: A page of VAT check history.

get.summary: Export VAT check history as CSV
get.description:
Downloads the account’s full VAT check history (all pages, not
paginated) as a CSV file, including the VIES consultation number
for each check. Returned as a file attachment.

200.description: The full VAT check history as a CSV file attachment.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment with a dated filename, e.g. `attachment; filename="vatnode-checks-2026-07-15.csv"`.

get.description:
Lists the account’s live API keys (previews only, never the full
secret) plus the current test key and the plan’s key limit.

post.description:
Mints a new live API key. The full secret is returned exactly once in
this response and never again – store it securely.

201.description: The created key, including the full secret (shown once).

422.description: The plan’s API-key limit has been reached (`KEY_LIMIT_REACHED`).

delete.description: Revokes (soft-deletes) a live API key. The key stops working immediately.

post.description:
Revokes (soft-deletes) a live API key. Equivalent outcome to
`DELETE /v1/me/api-keys/{id}`.
Issues a fresh test key, replacing the previous one.

get.summary: Should the welcome modal be shown?

200.description: Whether the onboarding welcome modal should be displayed.

post.description:
Marks the onboarding modal as seen (idempotent). Any provided answers
are emailed to the vatnode team; there is no persisted answer store.

get.description:
The merchant’s own EU VAT, attached as the `requester` on VIES calls
so responses carry a consultation number.

200.description: The configured requester (both fields null when unset).

patch.summary: Set or clear the account-level VIES requester
patch.description:
Sets the merchant’s own EU VAT (verified against VIES before saving)
or clears it. Accepts either a single full `vatId` or the split
`requesterCountryCode` + `requesterVatNumber` form. Pass
`{ "vatId": null }` to clear.

requesterCountryCode.description: Two-letter EU country code (VIES `EL` for Greece).

400.description:
Invalid VAT format (`INVALID_FORMAT`), VIES does not recognise the
number as active (`VIES_NOT_REGISTERED`), or the request body did
not match either accepted shape (`INVALID_REQUEST`).

get.description: All non-cancelled VAT-monitoring subscriptions for the account.

200.description: The account’s monitoring subscriptions and plan limit.

post.description:
Starts monitoring a VAT ID. Enforces per-plan limits and rejects
duplicates of an already-monitored VAT ID.

400.description:
The VAT ID does not parse to a valid format (`INVALID_FORMAT`), or
the request body failed structural validation – e.g. `vatId`
missing or outside 4–20 characters (`INVALID_REQUEST`).

403.description:
Monitoring is not available on the current plan or the plan’s
subscription limit has been reached (`PLAN_LIMIT`).

409.description: This VAT ID is already being monitored (`ALREADY_EXISTS`).

post.description:
Registers a new webhook endpoint. The URL must be a publicly
reachable HTTPS endpoint (validated against SSRF). The signing
`secret` is returned exactly once in this response. New webhooks start
`disabled` and are activated only after a successful test delivery
(`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test`).

201.description: The created webhook, including the signing secret (shown once).

422.description:
The URL is not a safe public HTTPS endpoint (`INVALID_URL`), or the
plan’s webhook limit has been reached / webhooks are unavailable on
the plan (`WEBHOOK_LIMIT_REACHED`).

get.description: A single webhook with its 20 most recent delivery attempts.

200.description: The webhook and its recent deliveries.

patch.description:
Update the URL and/or status. A webhook cannot be set `active`
directly – it must pass a test (`TEST_REQUIRED`). Changing the URL
drops the webhook back to `disabled` and requires a fresh test.

status.description: Only `disabled` is accepted; activation happens via a test.

422.description:
Attempted to set `active` directly (`TEST_REQUIRED`) or the URL is
not a safe public HTTPS endpoint (`INVALID_URL`).

delete.description:
Soft-deletes (deactivates) a webhook endpoint. The row is retained for
delivery history but stops counting against the plan’s webhook limit,
so the slot is free immediately.

post.description:
Sends a signed `webhook.test` event to the endpoint and returns the
live result (status code, latency, error) without persisting it to
delivery history. A successful (2xx) test is the only way a webhook
becomes `active`.

200.description:
The live test result. `ok` is true only for a 2xx response from the
endpoint; transport failures return `ok: false` with a null status
code and an `error` message.

get.description: The 50 most recent delivery attempts for a webhook, newest-first.

200.description: Recent delivery attempts for the webhook.

post.description:
Sent when a monitored VAT ID transitions from invalid → valid in VIES.
Delivered as a signed HTTP POST to every active webhook URL registered
on the account.

2XX.description: Acknowledged. Any 2xx status is treated as successful delivery.

post.description: Sent when a monitored VAT ID transitions from valid → invalid in VIES.

Sent when the company name returned by VIES for a monitored VAT ID
differs from the previously-recorded name. Fires only while the VAT ID
is currently valid.

Sent when the company address returned by VIES for a monitored VAT ID
differs from the previously-recorded address. Fires only while the
VAT ID is currently valid.

Sent at 23:00 UTC when every retry attempt (hourly between 06:00 and
22:00 UTC) failed to reach VIES for this subscription. The previous
recorded state of the VAT ID is unchanged – this event signals only
that the daily check could not complete.

RateLimitLimit.description:
Your plan’s monthly base quota. Emitted for live keys on both `200`
and `429` responses; omitted for unlimited (enterprise/internal) plans
and in test mode. Uses the IETF draft `RateLimit-*` header names.

RateLimitRemaining.description:
Requests remaining in the current monthly window after this request.
Computed as `max(limit - used - 1, 0)` – the current request has already
reserved its slot.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix epoch seconds at which the current monthly quota window resets.

VatnodeQuotaWarning.description:
Soft warning emitted only on `200` responses once usage reaches ~80% or
more of the monthly quota (and the request was still allowed). A human
hint for logs/monitoring, e.g. `82% of monthly quota used; upgrade at
https://vatnode.dev/dashboard/billing`. Absent below the threshold.

schema.example: 82% of monthly quota used; upgrade at https://vatnode.dev/dashboard/billing

ApiKey.description:
API key issued from the vatnode dashboard. Live keys (prefix
`vat_live_`) hit VIES and consume monthly quota. Test keys (prefix
`vat_test_`) accept only VAT IDs starting with `XX` and return
deterministic fixtures.

SessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
SessionCookie.description:
better-auth session cookie set when a user logs in to the dashboard.
Authenticates the account-management endpoints (`/v1/me/*`), which do
not accept API-key bearer tokens, and is one of the two accepted
credentials on `/v1/subscriptions/*` and `/v1/webhooks/*`.

VatIdPath.name: vatId
VatIdPath.description:
VAT ID including the two-letter country prefix as accepted by VIES,
e.g. `IE6388047V`. Greek VAT IDs must use the `EL` prefix – the ISO
code `GR` is **not** a valid VAT prefix and returns `INVALID_FORMAT`.
Northern Ireland uses `XI`. Whitespace and separators are normalised
server-side; no country-prefix aliasing is performed.

BulkJobIdPath.name: jobId
BulkJobIdPath.description: Bulk job identifier, as returned by `POST /v1/vat/bulk`.

WebhookSignatureHeader.name: X-Vatnode-Signature
WebhookSignatureHeader.description:
HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw request body>`, keyed with the full
per-webhook signing key (`vat_wh_…`, prefix included), formatted as
`t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex-hmac>`. Verify it before trusting the payload.

WebhookEventHeader.name: X-Vatnode-Event
WebhookEventHeader.description: The event type, mirroring the `event` field in the body.

SessionRequired.description: No valid session (`UNAUTHORIZED`), or the account has been deleted (`ACCOUNT_DELETED`).

NotFound.description:
The addressed resource does not exist, or is not owned by the
authenticated caller. Returns the standard error envelope with code
`NOT_FOUND`. Ownership and existence are deliberately not
distinguished, so a resource belonging to another account is reported
as missing rather than forbidden.

ValidationError.description:
The request body, query string or path parameters failed structural
validation (wrong type, missing required field, out-of-range length,
malformed enum, etc.). Returns the standard error envelope with code
`INVALID_REQUEST`. This is distinct from a semantically well-formed
request that is rejected later (e.g. `INVALID_FORMAT` for a VAT ID that
parses but is not a valid VAT number).

InternalError.description:
An unexpected server error occurred. Returns the standard error
envelope with code `INTERNAL_ERROR` and a `requestId` for support
correlation. The failing request had no side effects the caller can
rely on; retry is safe for idempotent operations.

used.description: How many the account currently has.

limit.description: How many the plan allows. `-1` = unlimited, `0` = not available on this plan.

valid.description:
Whether the VAT ID is valid. With `source: VIES` this is the VIES
verdict. With a national registry `source` it is that register’s
answer about domestic VAT registration, not a VIES confirmation
that the number is valid for intra-EU transactions – re-check in
VIES before relying on it to zero-rate an intra-EU supply.

countryCode.description: Two-letter country code extracted from the VAT ID.

registryCode.description:
The company’s number in the national business register, in its
national format (e.g. `0112038-9` for a Finnish Y-tunnus, `123 456 789`
for a French SIREN). Read off the VAT number where the VAT number is
built from it (BE, BG, CZ, DK, FI, FR, SE) and taken from the national
register for LT. `null` everywhere else, and for VAT numbers built
from a personal number (a Bulgarian ЕГН, a Czech rodné číslo, a
Swedish personnummer).

registryCodeName.description:
Local name of `registryCode` in the country’s first official
language (e.g. `Y-tunnus`, `numéro SIREN`). `null` when
`registryCode` is `null`.

taxId.description:
The national tax number the VAT number carries, in its national
format – e.g. the Spanish NIF, the Polish NIP, the Greek ΑΦΜ, or
`CZ` + IČO for a Czech DIČ. The same value as `registryCode` where
one number serves both (BE, DK, FI, FR, SE). `null` where the VAT
number is not the national tax number.

taxIdName.description:
Local name of `taxId` in the country’s first official language
(e.g. `NIP`, `ΑΦΜ`). `null` when `taxId` is `null`.

commercialName.description:
Trade / commercial name where the source provides one distinct from
the legal `companyName`. `null` when the source has only one name or
no commercial name (never a duplicate of `companyName`).

companyStatus.description:
Best-effort normalized operational status from the source registry
(one of `active`, `inactive`, `ceased`, `bankrupt`, `liquidation`,
`dissolved`, or a lowercased source value that does not map cleanly).
Enrichment metadata only – it never overrides `valid`. `null` when
the source provides no status.

secondaryActivities.description:
Secondary activity / classification descriptions where the source
provides them (the main activity is `industryDescription`). Empty
array when none or unavailable.

companyAgeYears.description:
Full years between `companyRegistrationDate` and `verifiedAt`
(floored). `null` when `companyRegistrationDate` is `null`.

registryPrivacy.description:
`true` when the source national register marks the record as
restricted from publication at the registrant’s own request – French
‘non-diffusible’, Dutch *afscherming*. The record above is still
returned in full; the flag tells you the registrant asked their
register not to hand these details out, which matters if you plan to
republish them. vatnode’s own public /check pages mask a flagged
record. `false` for every other result, including countries whose
register exposes no such flag.

checkId.description:
UUIDv7 identifier for this validation, and the primary key of the
stored check record. It is issued only after that record is
committed, so a `checkId` you hold always names a check vatnode can
still produce – it is a receipt, not a request id. If the record
cannot be stored, the response is `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED` (HTTP 502)
with no `checkId` and no quota consumed.

source.description:
Which system produced this result.

- `VIES` — the EU Commission’s VIES service answered directly. The
  only source that can carry a `consultationNumber`.
- `CACHE` — the base validation was served from vatnode’s cache
  (a prior VIES or national-register result, up to 15 minutes old).
  A cached result does not say which of the two produced it. Never
  carries a consultation number.
- A national registry code (`MF_PL` for PL, `ANAF_RO` for RO,
  `ARES_CZ` for CZ) – vatnode answered from that national register
  instead of VIES, either because VIES was unavailable for the
  country or, for some member states (currently CZ), because the
  register answered before VIES.
  `valid` then reflects the national register (domestic
  VAT registration), not a VIES confirmation that the number is
  valid for intra-EU transactions. Only possible when no requester
  was supplied; never carries a consultation number. The other
  national codes in the enum are not returned as a validity source.

A successful requester-authenticated call (one returning a
`consultationNumber`) always has `source: VIES`, because national
fallback is disabled whenever a requester is supplied.

consultationNumber.description:
VIES `requestIdentifier`, returned only when the account has a
requester VAT configured (dashboard Account details) and VIES answered
successfully via `checkVatApprox`. `null` when no requester is
configured, when the answer came from a national register, or when
served from cache.

specialTerritory.description:
The EU special-VAT territory the trader address falls in, or `null`.
Always present on the response; `null` for the overwhelming majority
of results – mainland traders, and every result whose source
returned no address to read.

SpecialTerritory.description:
An EU special-VAT territory whose treatment diverges from its member
state’s – the Canary Islands (IGIC, not VAT), the French overseas
departments, Åland, Madeira and the Azores among them.

**This is inferred from the address, not a tax determination.** No
special territory has its own VIES prefix: a Canary Islands business
carries an ordinary `ES` number and an Åland business an ordinary `FI`
one, so the only signal is a postal code in the trader address that
falls in a range exclusive to the territory. It reflects the registered
address, never the place of supply that governs any given transaction.

memberState.description: Parent member state’s VIES country prefix.

euVatArea.description:
`false` — outside the EU VAT area, under its own regime (Canary
IGIC) or behind a fiscal border (Åland). `true` – inside the EU VAT
area but on regional rates (Madeira, Azores).

source.description:
Provenance. Always `ADDRESS_INFERRED` – the value exists only
because a postal code was read out of the trader address.

vatNumberPattern.description: Regular expression the VAT number should match.

countryVatUpdatedAt.description: Date the rate dataset was last updated (ISO 8601).

LocalizedName.description: A name keyed by ISO 639-1 language code – every official language of the country, plus `en`. `null` where no official name could be confirmed.

CountryIdentifiers.description: Names, never numbers, of the country’s company registrar, company register, register number, business tax number and VAT identification number.

isEU.description: Whether the country is an EU member state. Non-EU countries are reference rates only – VAT number validation covers EU-27 + Northern Ireland.

updatedAt.description: Date the rate dataset was last updated (ISO 8601).

items.description:
A VAT ID in the usual `CC` + national-number form. Normalised
(trimmed, uppercased) before the batch is recorded.

vatIds.description:
The VAT IDs to validate. De-duplicated after normalisation, so
repeated entries yield one position and cost one quota unit.

status.description:
`queued` for a batch just accepted. A replay under an
`Idempotency-Key` returns the existing job, which may have moved on
already – including to one of the terminal states described on
`BulkJob`.

totalItems.description: Unique VAT IDs recorded – the number of positions the job has.

duplicatesDropped.description:
Entries removed as duplicates of an earlier one in the same batch.
On a fresh accept this is counted off the list you just sent; on a
replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` and batch it is the count the
original accept stored, not recomputed from this request.

status.description:
`finished` means every position has an answer – including positions
that answered with an error. It is not a claim that every VAT ID
was successfully validated; read `summary`.

`cancelled` means the job stopped early: positions it had already
answered keep their results, the rest stay `pending` and unbilled.

`failed` also means the job stopped early, for a reason of its own
rather than a stop it was asked for; `errorCode` says which.
Positions are treated exactly as under `cancelled`.

All three are terminal. Branch on the terminal set, not on
`finished` alone, so a job that ends any other way does not leave a
poller running until the job expires.

cancelRequestedAt.description:
When a cancel was first requested; the job may still be stopping.
A `cancelled` job can have this `null` – it was stopped by something
other than a cancel request, and `errorCode` says what.

expiresAt.description:
When the job and its positions are deleted (30 days after
submission). The underlying checks remain in your check history.

errorCode.description:
Why the job ended the way it did, when that needs saying. `null` for
an ordinary run and for a cancel you requested. `API_KEY_REVOKED`
means the API key the job was submitted with was revoked while it
was running, so it stopped where it stood.

position.description: 0-based index in submit order, after de-duplication.

status.description:
`pending` while the job is still working through the batch – and
permanently, on a `cancelled` job, for the positions it never
reached. Those were not checked and not charged.

valid.description:
`true`/`false` once a determination was reached, `null` while
pending or when the position failed – in which case `error` is set.

consultationNumber.description:
VIES `requestIdentifier`, present only when the account had a
requester VAT configured when the job was submitted.

checkId.description:
Receipt for the stored check behind this position – the same
identifier the single-ID endpoint returns. `null` for a position
that produced no verdict.

error.description: Present only for a failed position. The job itself still finishes.

code.description:
Per-position error code, same taxonomy as the single-ID
endpoint (`INVALID_FORMAT`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `VIES_UNAVAILABLE`,
`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `INVALID_REQUESTER`, `VIES_ERROR`,
`AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`).

VatSource.description:
Which system produced a result. `VIES` is the only source that can
carry a `consultationNumber`; `CACHE` is a prior result up to 15
minutes old; anything else is a national register used as fallback
when VIES was unavailable, whose verdict reflects domestic VAT
registration and is not a VIES confirmation.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code.

- `INVALID_REQUEST` — request body, query or path parameters failed structural validation. HTTP 400.
- `INVALID_FORMAT` — format invalid (local or VIES). HTTP 400.
- `INVALID_REQUESTER` — requester VAT is invalid in VIES. Only raised when a requester is supplied. HTTP 422.
- `UNAUTHORIZED` — Authorization header missing. HTTP 401.
- `INVALID_API_KEY` — API key is invalid or revoked. HTTP 401.
- `RATE_LIMITED` — monthly quota exceeded. HTTP 429.
- `VIES_UNAVAILABLE` — VIES/MS down; fallbacks also failed (no requester) or were skipped (requester set). HTTP 503.
- `VIES_ERROR` — unexpected VIES protocol error (incl. `VAT_BLOCKED` / `IP_BLOCKED` at HTTP 403, and a requester-qualified `valid: true` that carried no consultation number). HTTP 502 or 403.
- `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` — VIES request timed out and no fallback was available. HTTP 504.
- `AUDIT_WRITE_FAILED` — the check ran, but its audit record could not be stored, so no `checkId` was issued and the verdict is withheld. Not counted against your quota; safe to retry. HTTP 502.
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` — unhandled server error. HTTP 500.
- `NOT_FOUND` — unknown country code (rates only). HTTP 404.

requestId.description: Echoes the `X-Request-Id` header for support correlation.

viesCode.description: Raw VIES error code when the underlying failure came from VIES.

id.description:
Stable, unique identifier for the event. Identical across every retry
of the same delivery – use it to deduplicate.

version.description:
Envelope schema version. Currently `1`. Bumped only on a breaking
change to the payload shape, so consumers can version-handle safely.

event.description: Event type. See per-envelope schema for allowed values.

timestamp.description: When the event was emitted (ISO-8601, UTC).

vatId.description:
The monitored VAT ID, including the VAT prefix as accepted by VIES.
Greek VAT IDs always use the `EL` prefix (e.g. `EL123456789`) – this
is the only valid prefix for Greece.

countryCode.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (the code used for VAT-rate lookups).
For Greece this is `GR`, while the `vatId` above carries the `EL`
prefix – `EL` is the VAT prefix, `GR` is the rates code. Northern
Ireland is `XI`.

subscriptionId.description: Stable identifier of the subscription this event belongs to.

ManagementError.description:
Error envelope for the account-management endpoints. Shares the shape
of `VatError` but carries a broader, endpoint-specific set of `code`
values.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code. Common values across the
account-management endpoints:

- `UNAUTHORIZED` — no valid session. HTTP 401.
- `ACCOUNT_DELETED` — the account has been soft-deleted. HTTP 401.
- `DB_UNAVAILABLE` — database temporarily unavailable. HTTP 503.
- `INVALID_REQUEST` — request body/query/path failed structural validation. HTTP 400.
- `INVALID_FORMAT` — invalid VAT ID format. HTTP 400.
- `NOT_FOUND` — resource missing or not owned by the caller. HTTP 404.
- `ALREADY_EXISTS` — VAT ID already monitored. HTTP 409.
- `ALREADY_DELETED` — account already scheduled for deletion. HTTP 409.
- `PLAN_LIMIT` — plan feature/limit reached (subscriptions). HTTP 403.
- `KEY_LIMIT_REACHED` — plan API-key limit reached. HTTP 422.
- `WEBHOOK_LIMIT_REACHED` — plan webhook limit reached / unavailable. HTTP 422.
- `INVALID_URL` — webhook URL is not a safe public HTTPS endpoint. HTTP 422.
- `TEST_REQUIRED` — a webhook must pass a test before activation. HTTP 422.
- `VIES_NOT_REGISTERED` — VIES does not recognise the requester VAT. HTTP 400.
- `CREATION_FAILED` / `REGENERATION_FAILED` / `INTERNAL_ERROR` – server-side failure. HTTP 500.

requestId.description: Present on most errors; echoes the `X-Request-Id` header.

used.description: Requests used in the current billing period.

total.description: Lifetime request total across all of the account’s keys.

remaining.description: Remaining inside the included quota (clamped at 0). `-1` when unlimited.

limit.description: Plan subscription limit. `-1` means unlimited, `0` means unavailable.

email.description: Override alert address. Empty string means ‘use the account email’.

key.description: The full API key secret. Returned only once, at creation.

limit.description: Plan subscription limit. `-1` means unlimited, `0` means unavailable.

consecutiveFailures.description: Consecutive failed deliveries. Present on list/update responses.

status.description: New webhooks start disabled until a test delivery succeeds.

secret.description: HMAC signing key. Returned only once, at creation.

nextRetryAt.description: Present only on the deliveries-list endpoint.

ok.description: True only for a 2xx response from the endpoint.

request.description: The request that was sent (method, URL, headers, body).

response.description: The endpoint’s response (headers, body), or null on transport failure.

tags.name: VAT validation
tags.description: Validate EU VAT IDs against VIES with national fallback.

tags.name: VAT rates
tags.description: Up-to-date VAT rates for EU member states.

tags.name: Account summary
tags.description: Plan, quota, monitoring and billing state for the account a key belongs to.

tags.name: Account
tags.description:
Session-authenticated account management: profile, usage, API keys,
notification settings and the account-level VIES requester. Used by the
vatnode dashboard.

tags.name: Monitoring subscriptions
tags.description:
CRUD for VAT-monitoring subscriptions, authenticated by the dashboard
session or a live API key. Each
subscription re-validates a VAT ID against VIES on a daily schedule and
emits webhook events on state changes.

tags.name: Webhook management
tags.description:
CRUD for the webhook endpoints that receive
monitoring events, plus test delivery and delivery-history inspection.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Event deliveries from VAT monitoring subscriptions. vatnode POSTs a
signed JSON payload to every URL you register in the dashboard whenever
a monitored VAT ID changes state (or once at 23:00 UTC if VIES was
unreachable for the full day).
